title: Separated cycling network extension in Waterloo and Kitchener
subtitle: Kissing Bridge Trailway pedestrian bridge, Oxford Road 5 transfer, all-way stop, Weber Street speed limit, climate plan update
overview: The committee recommended approving preferred designs for separated cycling routes on King Street, University Avenue, Bridgeport Road, Caroline Street and Erb Street East {{vote:m4}}. Staff said the designs add protected space for cyclists and wider sidewalks, with lane reductions on several streets. Delegates in favour included a school travel planning team and a cycling advocacy group. Staff noted that individual projects still come back separately and that pending provincial legislation could require ministerial approval for some lane removals.

The committee also recommended moving ahead with a pedestrian bridge over the Conestogo River on the Kissing Bridge Trailway {{vote:m5}}. It would advance construction to 2025 and 2026 and add a two-year contract project manager. Staff are to return to Council if the Region's net share is expected to exceed $500,000. It further recommended starting the transfer of three Oxford Road 5 segments in Wilmot Township to the Region, with up to $200,000 for safety work at the Punkeydoodles intersection {{vote:m6}}.

Through the consent agenda {{vote:m1}}, it recommended an all-way stop at Fischer-Hallman and Roseville roads and a lower speed limit on part of Weber Street. It received a corporate climate action plan update for information. Council will consider these recommendations later.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the current preferred alternative designs for separated cycling facilities on King Street, University Avenue, Bridgeport Road, Caroline Street and Erb Street East, as set out in report TSD-TRP-24-015.

The committee recommended advancing the Conestogo River crossing to 2025/2026 with a revised budget, funding agreements, an immediate environmental assessment start, a return to Council if the Region's net share is expected to exceed $500,000, and a two-year contract project manager.

The committee recommended starting the process to transfer three road segments from Wilmot Township to the Region, and approving an upset limit of $200,000 for safety improvements at the Punkeydoodles intersection.

decisions.item: All-way stop at Fischer-Hallman and Roseville
decisions.detail: Through the consent agenda, the committee recommended installing an all-way stop at Fischer-Hallman Road and Roseville Road in North Dumfries and amending the Traffic and Parking By-law accordingly.
Through the consent agenda, the committee recommended reducing the posted speed limit on Weber Street between Allen Street and 20 m south of King Street in Waterloo to 50 km/h.

debate: Delegates supporting the cycling network said protected lanes make streets safer and more comfortable for children, seniors and families, give students safer routes to school, and may reduce household car use and costs. One asked staff to consider wider lanes, continuous crosswalks, floating bus stops and trees.

A cycling advocacy delegate questioned why cycling facilities would be last in snow clearing and urged giving active transportation projects priority when budget deferrals are discussed. The delegate also criticized pending provincial Bill 212 as a threat to local decisions.

Councillors raised concerns about e-bike speed and weight on shared facilities, driver and cyclist education, and whether a height difference between sidewalk and cycle track could be a tripping hazard. Staff said a flush design is currently proposed, details will be set in design, and the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee is to be consulted.

Staff said lane reductions would add roughly a minute or more to some peak trips, for example on Herb Street, but could slow traffic speeds. Some councillors pressed for further study of two-way traffic on Bridgeport and Herb; staff said that study will continue.

On the Kissing Bridge bridge, councillors asked about debt, grant risk and the new position. Staff said it would be a contract role tied to the project, funding agreements would recover environmental assessment costs, and an assessment stays valid for 10 years if the project is deferred.
